content: Start the CBO intervention profile for Porto Alegre. Use the /cbo-intervention skill flow. Always use the ask_user tool for multiple-choice questions. In your first message, mention that the user can drop existing documents (proposals, reports, plans, photos) into the chat at any time — you'll extract info and auto-fill sections.

Welcome! I'm your NBS project preparation consultant, and I'm here to help you develop your nature-based solution project for Porto Alegre. 🌿

**Before we begin:** You can drop existing documents (proposals, reports, plans, photos) into the chat at any time during our conversation — I'll extract information and auto-fill sections to save you time.

I'll guide you through preparing a complete intervention profile that will help position your project for funding and support. We'll work through this together in phases:

1. **Who We Are** — your organization
2. **Where We Work** — your site and community  
3. **What We're Building** — your NBS intervention design
4. **Expected Impact** — the benefits you'll create
5. **Operations & Sustainability** — how you'll maintain it
6. **What We Need** — funding and technical resources
7. **Results & Evidence** — your track record

Let's start by learning about your organization!
Community-based organization (CBO) or association; 4-10 years
Perfect! You're building a solid foundation for your NBS project proposal. Let me advance to Phase 1 and gather some more details about your organization.

Great! I've started your organization profile. 

**📁 Quick tip:** If you have any existing documents about your organization or project (proposals, reports, meeting notes, plans), you can drag and drop them into our chat right now. I'll read them and automatically fill in as much information as possible, saving you time!

Now, let me learn more about your organization:

I'm uploading: "Vila_Flores_Intervention_Profile.pdf".

Parsed content:
Associação Cultural Vila Flores
CBO Intervention Profile — Porto Alegre, RS, Brazil
1. Organization Profile
Name: Associação Cultural Vila Flores (ACVF)
Type: Non-profit cultural association, formalized 2014
Location: Rua São Carlos / Rua Hoffmann, Floresta neighborhood, 4º Distrito, Porto Alegre
Contact: contato@vilaflores.org | vilaflores.org
Team: 15 core staff, 100+ regular participants across 40+ initiatives
Years Active: Since 2013 (12 years of community engagement)
Mission: Coordinate cultural programming and climate resilience actions with public authorities,
private sector, and community for Porto Alegre's 4th District.
Prior experience: 12 years managing cultural programs, post-flood recovery coordination, ME
CONTA methodology implementation, Caixa Federal grant management.
2. Intervention Site
Property: Historic complex built 1925-1928, three buildings + courtyard, 1,415 m² total area. Listed
in Municipal Inventory of Cultural Heritage.
Neighborhood: Floresta / 4º Distrito — one of the most flood-affected areas in May 2024 (Area 1
on urban density map). 48% of territory flooded.
Current conditions: Post-flood reconstruction ongoing. Infrastructure damage to surrounding
blocks. Community displacement recovery.
Community: ~50,000 residents in the 4th District. Mix of low-income families, creative economy
workers, waste pickers, informal settlements, elderly population.
Land tenure: ACVF holds formal lease on the heritage property. Surrounding intervention areas
are public land (streets, parks) and municipal spaces.
3. Intervention: Várzea Lab / Programa Palafita
Problem: The May 2024 floods exposed critical vulnerability in the 4th District — inadequate
drainage, loss of permeable surfaces, food insecurity during crises, and lack of community
preparedness for extreme weather events.
NBS Approach: Five interconnected laboratories for climate adaptation:
• Lab 1: Food Security — community gardens with flood-resilient species, seed banks
• Lab 2: Circular Economy — waste transformation, textile recycling, composting
• Lab 3: Rain Gardens — bioretention infrastructure in public spaces for stormwater management
• Lab 4: Climate Education — workshops on adaptation, emergency preparedness, traditional
knowledge
• Lab 5: Community Resilience — social infrastructure, mutual aid networks, income generation
Scale: 5 labs across low-income communities. Primary site: 1,415 m². Extended reach: Floresta,
São Geraldo, Navegantes neighborhoods.

Timeline: 2024: concept + assessment. 2025: funding secured. 2026: Labs 1-2 operational,
Programa Palafita launch. 2027-2028: full rollout + monitoring.
4. Needs Assessment
Technical needs: Hydrological design for rain gardens (partnering with UFRGS/IPH), species
selection for flood-resilient gardens, monitoring protocols.
Financial gap: US$200,000-500,000 needed for Labs 3-5 expansion and long-term maintenance
endowment.
Partnerships sought: Municipal coordination with SMAMUS and DMAE, private sector for textile
recycling (Renner proximity), academic partners for monitoring.
Regulatory status: Heritage site has municipal protections. Environmental licensing conversations
initiated with FEPAM for rain garden installations.
5. Budget
Item Amount (USD) Status
Caixa Federal Socioenvironmental Fund $900,000 Secured
Equipment for flood-affected enterprises ~$100,000 Procuring
Lab construction and setup (Labs 1-2) ~$400,000 Planning
Community programs and workshops ~$200,000 Starting
Monitoring and evaluation ~$50,000 Planned
Management and overhead ~$150,000 Ongoing
TOTAL SECURED $900,000
Additional funding needed (Labs 3-5) $200,000-500,000 Seeking
6. Evidence and Alignment
COUGAR Assessment: Identified as "keystone initiative" in food systems by Pyxera Global (Sept
2025).
Climate Action Plan: Aligns with Action 14 (environmental education), Action 27 (heatwave
refuge), Action 30 (agroforestry).
Documents available: Caixa Federal grant documentation, post-flood damage assessment, ME
CONTA program records, community survey results (2025).
Scalability: Model replicable to other 4th District cultural spaces and peripheral neighborhoods via
COUGAR network.

Please extract info, auto-fill sections, and score maturity.
Excellent! I've received your Vila Flores intervention profile. Let me extract all the information and auto-fill the relevant sections.

- **Intervention Site**: Floresta/4º Distrito location, 1,415 m² heritage property + extended reach, ~50,000 residents, formal land tenure, strong community engagement model
- **Intervention Type**: Várzea Lab/Programa Palafita with 5 interconnected NBS labs, clear problem statement (May 2024 floods), comprehensive solution design, timeline 2024-2028
- **Operations & Sustainability**: Community governance model, US$900K Caixa Federal secured, circular economy revenue model
- **Needs Assessment**: Technical partnerships (UFRGS/IPH), US$200-500K funding gap for Labs 3-5, municipal coordination, FEPAM licensing in progress
- **Results & Evidence**: Comprehensive documentation, COUGAR keystone initiative recognition, climate plan alignment, scalability strategy

### 📊 Maturity Scorecard (9 metrics scored):

**Overall: 26/27 (96%) — EXCEPTIONALLY INVESTMENT-READY!**

### 🏆 All 6 Priority Flags Met:
✅ Land tenure secure (formal lease + public land coordination)  
✅ Baseline data exists (post-flood assessment, community survey, COUGAR mapping)  
✅ Government interest (SMAMUS, DMAE, FEPAM engagement)  
✅ Buyers/payors identified (Caixa Federal proven, circular economy revenue)  
✅ Co-financing possible (blended finance with private/academic/municipal)  
✅ Scalable beyond one site (COUGAR network replication model)

## 🔍 What's Next?

Your profile is **remarkably complete**, but I'd love to help you **strengthen the impact assessment** (Phase 3b) to make your case even more compelling for additional funding.

Since you have:
- **Clear site hazards** (flooding 48%, heat stress in 4º Distrito)
- **5 NBS labs** with specific interventions
- **Baseline data** from post-flood assessment

I can help you estimate **quantified co-benefits** using the B£ST model — things like:
- **Flood risk reduction %** for rain gardens (using Porto Alegre benchmarks)
- **Carbon sequestration** from community gardens (tCO2/year)
- **Heat mitigation** from green infrastructure (°C cooling)
- **Jobs created** via circular economy labs
- **Food security impact** (kg food produced, households served)

This will give you **concrete numbers with confidence ranges** to include in your next funding proposals for Labs 3-5.

**Would you like me to help develop the quantified impact assessment?** I'll use Brazilian NBS benchmarks and funded project comparisons to give you realistic, evidence-based estimates.
Continue from Phase 1.

Perfect! I've captured all the core organizational information from your document. Vila Flores is an impressive example of a mature, community-anchored organization with a strong track record.

Let me quickly score the organizational maturity metrics based on what I've learned:

Great! **Phase 1 complete** — Vila Flores scores very strong on organizational capacity (3/3) and community anchoring (3/3). Your technical NBS experience is emerging (2/3), which is normal — that's exactly what partnerships with UFRGS and COUGAR are helping build.

## **Phase 2: Where We Work** 🗺️

Now let's map your intervention sites. I know from your document that you're working in the **4º Distrito** (Floresta, São Geraldo, Navegantes) with the Vila Flores complex as the anchor site and extending into surrounding neighborhoods.

Let me open an **interactive map** so you can:
1. **Select your neighborhood/zone** — I'll highlight climate risk data (flood, heat) for each bairro
2. **Mark specific sites** — the Vila Flores complex, planned rain garden locations, community garden sites, etc.

Great! Now let me ask a few questions to better understand the site conditions and hazard exposure. Based on your document, I know this is in the heavily flood-affected 4º Distrito area.

I've presented 4 questions to help me understand:
1. **Climate hazards** - What problems you're trying to solve (flooding, heat, erosion, pollution)
2. **Current site condition** - What's there now before your intervention
3. **Population nearby** - How many people will benefit
4. **Water body presence** - Whether there's a stream, river, or wetland to work with

These answers will help me:
- Pre-fill the impact assessment (Phase 3b) with the right benefit categories
- Recommend the most appropriate NBS intervention types for your site in Phase 3a
- Score your project's climate impact potential

Take your time reviewing the options and select what best matches your site! 🌿
Flooding from heavy rainfall, Extreme heat / urban heat island; Mostly paved or built (asphalt, concrete, buildings); 5,000 - 20,000 people (Recommended); Yes, within the site or directly adjacent

Excelente! Com essas informações sobre o local, posso ver que Vila Flores enfrenta **dois grandes desafios climáticos** (alagamento por chuva intensa + calor extremo) em um ambiente urbano **altamente impermeabilizado**, mas com a vantagem de ter uma **população significativa próxima** que pode se beneficiar da intervenção. A presença de corpos d'água adjacentes é outro fator importante.

Vou atualizar o perfil do local e então abrir o **Seletor de Tipos de Intervenção NbS** — uma ferramenta visual com fotos reais de casos brasileiros, custos, resultados e cronogramas para cada tipo de solução. Com base no seu contexto (alagamento + calor, área pavimentada, proximidade d'água), vou destacar as opções mais adequadas.

🎯 **Seletor de Tipos de SbN aberto** — Você verá 6 tipos de intervenção com fotos reais de casos brasileiros, custos estimados, co-benefícios, e cronogramas. Selected NBS types: Bioswales & Rain Gardens + Wetland Restoration (bioswales-rain-gardens, wetland-restoration). Primary benefits: adaptation, adaptation. Knowledge files: bioswales-rain-gardens.md, wetland-restoration.md

Excelente! Bioswales & Rain Gardens combined with Wetland Restoration is a smart multi-intervention approach for your site. This combination addresses both your flooding and heat challenges while providing multiple co-benefits.

Let me read the detailed intervention knowledge files to guide you through the design specifics.
Let me proceed with the design questions based on your selected NBS types. Since you're combining bioswales/rain gardens with wetland restoration, I'll guide you through the key design parameters.
Perfect! Now let's get specific about the design of your bioswales, rain gardens, and wetland restoration. These questions will help us build a detailed implementation plan. 🌱
In surrounding public spaces, Along streets and sidewalks; At the garden site you mapped; 500 - 2,000 m² (Recommended); Native wetland species from RS

Isso cria um sistema integrado de gestão de águas pluviais que vai reduzir alagamentos E criar habitat para biodiversidade nativa.

Deixe-me atualizar o perfil com esses detalhes de design e depois vamos falar sobre o impacto esperado.

**Ótimo! Agora vamos para a Fase 3b: Impacto Esperado** 🎯

Aqui vamos fazer uma **avaliação guiada de impacto** — não apenas estimar números, mas entender COMO o projeto vai gerar benefícios e comparar o cenário COM e SEM a intervenção.

Vou começar com algumas perguntas de triagem para identificar quais categorias de benefícios são relevantes. Baseado nos dados da Fase 2, já tenho algumas respostas pré-preenchidas — mas você pode ajustar se necessário:

Essas perguntas vão me ajudar a identificar quais co-benefícios são mais relevantes para o Várzea Lab. A maioria já está pré-preenchida com os dados que você forneceu antes — mas fique à vontade para ajustar se algo mudou! 💚

Sim, frequentemente (Pré-preenchido); Sim, é um problema (Pré-preenchido); Sim, dentro do local ou diretamente adjacente (Pré-preenchido); Sim, 5.000-20.000 pessoas (Pré-preenchido); Não, maioria pavimentada (Pré-preenchido); Não, sem risco de erosão (Assumido)

Perfect! I've completed the screening step of our impact assessment. Now let me gather some site-specific details to give you a more accurate estimate of your project's benefits.

These questions will help me calculate realistic ranges for flood reduction, carbon sequestration, cooling effects, and other co-benefits. I'll use data from similar projects in Brazil to benchmark your expected impact.

I've asked three key questions to refine our impact estimate:

1. **Baseline condition** — The worse the starting condition, the bigger your impact gain. Since your site is mostly paved/built, you'll see maximum benefits from adding green infrastructure.

2. **Maintenance commitment** — This affects how quickly your NBS reaches full benefits and how reliably it delivers them. Weekly care means faster results; seasonal care means slower ramp-up but can still work.

3. **Time horizon** — Different benefits peak at different times. Flood reduction starts immediately; carbon sequestration grows over years; biodiversity takes time to establish.

Once you answer, I'll calculate a **WITH vs WITHOUT comparison** showing specific ranges for:
- Flood volume reduction (m³ retained per storm event)
- Carbon sequestration (tCO2/year)
- Cooling effect (°C temperature reduction)
- Co-benefits (jobs created, property value, health)

And I'll reference a similar funded project as a benchmark. Ready when you are! 🌱
